coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the playing area into a defensive movement zone, midfield support zone and forward movement zone.
Use two balanced teams.
The defensive zone contains corridor, boundary and reset options.
The midfield zone rewards overlaps, give-and-go movement and effective support angles.
The forward zone rewards coordinated leading, holding and clearing.
Coaches hold spare footballs to create rapid turnover restarts.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins with possession in the defensive zone.
Players select movement lanes that support a controlled exit.
On reaching midfield, players decide whether to overlap, give-and-go, carry or remain connected.
Forward players decide whether to lead, hold width or clear space.
A successful scoring attempt is worth three points.
Teams receive one additional point for each correctly identified movement decision during the possession.
On turnover, both teams immediately reorganise into attacking and defensive lanes.
Coaches may restart with an imperfect football or from another zone.
Play in four-minute blocks with one-minute review periods.
Record decision quality separately from skill execution.
Rotate player positions between blocks.
Complete at least four assessment blocks.
coachingPoints: Scan before moving, not only before receiving.
Coordinate movement with teammates.
Maintain width, depth and support behind the football.
Overlap only when the defender commits.
Continue for a return possession only when released.
Carry the football when running improves the attack.
Lead, hold or clear according to the forward picture.
React immediately after turnovers.
Evaluate movement by the advantage it creates.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether movement begins from scanning.
Whether players maintain separation.
Whether overlap and give-and-go decisions are appropriate.
Whether support angles remain visible.
Whether ball carriers carry or release at the correct time.
Whether forward movement is coordinated.
Whether transition lanes are occupied quickly.
Whether fatigue reduces movement discipline.
Whether correct decisions are recognised despite execution errors.
progressions: Increase defensive pressure to full match intensity.
Remove all marked zones and lanes.
Start from stoppages, kick-ins and intercepted marks.
Require player leaders to organise movement.
Track individual movement decisions across multiple sessions.
regressions: Assess one zone at a time.
Give each player one movement focus.
Shorten work blocks to protect decision quality.
successIndicators: Select effective leads, holds and clearing runs.
Continue running after disposal when released.
Carry and release at effective times.
Explain how their movement created or protected advantage.
matchApplication: The assessment connects movement decisions across defensive exits, midfield ball movement, forward entries and turnovers. It measures whether players move with purpose according to the live game picture rather than following fixed patterns.

title: Stop, Turn or Release
primarySkill: Selecting the correct action while carrying the football
objective: Develop players’ ability to decide whether to continue running, stop and change direction, or release the football according to the defender’s closing angle and available support.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Position one ball carrier at the starting end.
Place one defender eight metres ahead and slightly to one side.
Position two supporting teammates in separate passing lanes.
Set a forward gate, a change-of-direction gate and a release target.
The defender may hold the forward lane, overcommit to one side or close directly towards the carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier receives from a feeder and advances into the area.
The defender selects a closing angle.
If the forward lane remains open, the carrier continues through the forward gate.
If the defender overcommits, the carrier stops, changes direction and exits through the opposite gate.
If the defender closes the carrier’s space, the player releases to an available supporting teammate.
Play continues through one additional disposal.
Attackers score one point for the correct decision and one point for successful execution.
The defender scores one point for forcing an error or turnover.
Rotate the carrier, defender and supporting roles.
Practise from both sides.
coachingPoints: Scan the defender’s hips, speed and closing angle.
Continue forward when space remains available.
Change direction only when the defender has committed.
Release before entering tackling distance.
Keep the football protected during stops and turns.
Supporting players must maintain separate lanes.
Reassess after every defender movement.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the carrier recognises the defender’s angle.
Whether players stop unnecessarily despite open space.
Whether changes of direction occur after defender commitment.
Whether the football is released before pressure traps the carrier.
Whether support players stay visible.
Whether the next disposal maintains advantage.
progressions: Require the carrier to bounce before the decision.
regressions: Walk through each decision before increasing intensity.
successIndicators: Protect the football throughout the action.
matchApplication: The drill reflects carrying possession through the midfield or away from congestion, where the player must continually assess whether to attack space, evade pressure or connect with support.

title: Receive, Run Through or Roll Out
objective: Teach players to decide whether to continue running through the receiving lane, roll away from pressure or stop and release immediately after taking possession.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Position a feeder at one end.
Place a receiver 12 metres away.
Set a continuation gate behind the receiver.
Mark a curved roll-out gate to one side.
Position one short-release target near the receive point.
A defender begins behind, beside or in front of the receiver.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver scans the defender before leading.
The feeder disposes to the receiver.
If the defender trails, the receiver continues running through the forward gate.
If the defender closes from the front, the receiver rolls away through the side gate.
If the defender arrives from the side and removes both movement lanes, the receiver releases immediately to support.
The receiver completes the next disposal after exiting.
One point is awarded for the correct movement choice.
One point is awarded for clean execution.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Scan the defender’s starting position and movement.
Receive at speed when the forward lane is safe.
Roll towards space, not merely away from contact.
Use the body to protect the football.
Release immediately when movement lanes are closed.
Keep the feet active during possession.
Prepare the disposal before completing the turn.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether scanning occurs before possession.
Whether the receiver maintains momentum when unpressured.
Whether the roll-out moves away from the defender.
Whether players stop unnecessarily.
Whether the quick-release option is used when required.
Whether the football remains secure.
regressions: Tell the receiver where pressure begins.
Practise one movement option at a time.
matchApplication: Players receiving through half-back, midfield or around stoppage must decide instantly whether to maintain momentum, evade pressure or move the football before being tackled.

title: Decoy Run Recognition
primarySkill: Recognising when to make or use a decoy run
objective: Develop players’ ability to use purposeful decoy movement to draw a defender and create space for a teammate without demanding unnecessary possession.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one ball carrier outside the attacking area.
Place two attacking targets and two defenders inside.
Mark a central leading lane and two wider receiving zones.
One attacker begins closer to the central lane.
The other begins deeper or wider.
Defenders may follow, switch or hold their position.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier receives and scans the attacking picture.
One attacker makes an aggressive lead into the central lane.
If a defender follows, the second attacker moves into the space created.
If the defender holds and leaves the first attacker free, the ball carrier may use the original lead.
The decoy runner must continue through the lane rather than stopping.
The ball carrier selects the player who gains the clearest advantage.
Play continues through one additional disposal or shot.
Attackers score two points when a decoy movement creates a successful possession.
Rotate attackers, defenders and ball carriers.
coachingPoints: A decoy run must be fast and believable.
Continue through the space so it remains available for the next player.
Do not call for possession if receiving would disadvantage the team.
The second attacker must delay movement until the defender reacts.
The ball carrier must still use the decoy runner if the defender does not follow.
Maintain separation between attacking movements.
Reassess if defenders switch opponents.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the decoy run attracts defensive attention.
Whether the runner clears the space fully.
Whether the second attacker times movement correctly.
Whether the ball carrier recognises defender reaction.
Whether attackers crowd the same lane.
Whether defenders communicate and switch.
progressions: Add a trailing midfielder entering late.
regressions: Freeze play after the first defensive reaction.
matchApplication: Decoy movement creates space in forward entries, stoppage exits and team offence by forcing defenders to choose between following one player and protecting another dangerous area.

title: Support Behind or Ahead
primarySkill: Selecting support position relative to the football
objective: Teach players to decide whether to provide support ahead of possession or remain behind the football according to numbers, pressure and turnover risk.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Use four attackers against three defenders.
One attacker begins with the football.
Place two attackers ahead and one supporting player behind.
Mark a forward scoring gate and a reset gate.
Defenders vary whether they press the ball carrier or drop behind the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier advances into the area.
The supporting player assesses numbers ahead and defensive pressure.
If attackers have an advantage and the defender commits, support may run ahead to create an extra option.
If numbers are even or the turnover risk is high, support remains behind the football.
The attacking team attempts to reach the forward gate.
If forward movement closes, the rear support may receive through the reset gate.
After a turnover, the rear support becomes important to defensive recovery.
Attackers score two points for a successful forward entry.
Defenders score two points for counterattacking through the reset gate.
Rotate roles after each passage.
coachingPoints: Count attackers and defenders before running ahead.
Maintain support behind when possession is unstable.
Run forward when the additional player creates a genuine advantage.
Do not leave every player ahead of the football.
Use depth to provide a safe reset.
Communicate who is holding behind.
Reassess immediately after every disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether support players recognise the numerical picture.
Whether too many attackers run ahead.
Whether a reset remains available.
Whether forward support creates an actual spare player.
Whether defensive balance is maintained.
Whether the rear player reacts after turnover.
regressions: Predetermine when support should stay behind.
successIndicators: Run ahead when it creates advantage.
matchApplication: Teams require players ahead of the football to attack and players behind it to support and defend turnover. The correct balance changes throughout every possession.

title: Split-Lane Movement Choice
primarySkill: Selecting between inside and outside movement lanes
objective: Develop players’ ability to select an inside or outside movement lane according to defender positioning, field space and the ball carrier’s angle.
groundSize: 20 × 30 metres divided into inside and outside lanes.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Mark an inside lane towards the corridor and an outside lane towards the boundary.
Position a ball carrier at one end.
Place one receiver and one defender in the central area.
Position a target beyond each lane.
The defender begins on either the inside or outside shoulder of the receiver.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver scans the defender’s position and the ball carrier’s angle.
If the defender protects the inside lane, the receiver leads outside.
If the defender sits outside, the receiver cuts through the inside lane.
The ball carrier delivers into the selected path.
The receiver takes possession and connects with the target beyond the lane.
The defender applies controlled tracking pressure.
One point is awarded for correct lane selection.
One point is awarded for receiving without slowing.
Rotate all roles and practise both sides.
coachingPoints: Scan the defender before committing to a lane.
Attack the shoulder that provides the clearest path.
Use the inside lane when it creates direct attacking advantage.
Use the outside lane when it protects possession and opens space.
Avoid drifting between lanes.
Accelerate once the defender’s position is recognised.
The ball carrier must deliver to advantage.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the receiver scans before movement.
Whether the chosen lane matches the defensive position.
Whether players hesitate between lanes.
Whether the lead is decisive.
Whether the ball carrier recognises the same decision.
Whether the receiver maintains momentum.
progressions: Allow the defender to switch shoulders during the lead.
regressions: Tell the receiver which shoulder is protected.
successIndicators: Select the correct inside or outside lane.
matchApplication: Receivers must continually choose whether to lead towards the corridor or boundary based on defender position, team structure and the ball carrier’s ability to access the lane.

title: Inside Runner or Outside Runner
primarySkill: Selecting the most effective running support lane
objective: Teach supporting players to choose an inside or outside running lane that complements the ball carrier and creates the greatest attacking advantage.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Use three attackers against two defenders.
One attacker begins as the ball carrier.
Two supporting runners begin behind and to either side.
Mark an inside gate near the corridor and an outside gate near the boundary.
Defenders vary their width and closing positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier advances towards the defenders.
Supporting runners scan the defensive shape and each other.
One runner selects the inside lane and the other holds outside width.
If the defenders compress centrally, the outside runner becomes the preferred option.
If defenders spread wide, the inside runner attacks the central gap.
The ball carrier draws a defender before releasing.
Attackers attempt to exit through either gate.
Two points are awarded for using the lane that best exploits the defensive shape.
Defenders counterattack after turnover.
Rotate all positions.
coachingPoints: Runners must occupy different lanes.
Hold outside width when central defenders compress.
Attack the inside gap when defenders separate.
Time the run so the ball carrier can draw pressure first.
Avoid crossing directly in front of another runner.
Communicate the selected lane.
Maintain defensive balance behind the play.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether runners select complementary lanes.
Whether the defensive shape is recognised.
Whether the preferred option changes correctly.
Whether runs begin too early.
Whether the ball carrier commits a defender.
Whether width and depth are maintained.
successIndicators: Select the lane offering the strongest advantage.
matchApplication: Inside and outside runners help teams move through defensive lines. Their value depends on reading defender spacing and creating complementary rather than duplicated movement.

title: Fold, Rotate or Hold Shape
objective: Develop players’ ability to decide whether to fold around possession, rotate into a vacated position or hold team shape after the football changes location.
groundSize: 35 × 45 metres divided into three channels and three depth lines.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use two teams of five to ten players.
Mark left, central and right channels.
Mark rear, middle and forward depth lines.
Begin one team in possession with players spread across the grid.
Defenders apply controlled pressure.
Players must maintain minimum width and at least one player behind the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team moves the football across the area.
After every disposal, the original ball carrier assesses the new team shape.
The player may fold around to become the next support option.
The player may rotate into a position vacated by a teammate.
The player may hold position when movement would damage width, depth or defensive balance.
Teams score one point for five consecutive disposals while maintaining shape.
An additional point is awarded for penetrating a target gate.
Defenders score for turnovers or forcing three attackers into one channel.
Play continues immediately after turnovers.
Review shape between two-minute blocks.
coachingPoints: Movement after disposal must solve a structural need.
Fold around when the next possession requires support.
Rotate when a teammate vacates an important lane.
Hold position when width or defensive balance would otherwise disappear.
Maintain at least one player behind the football.
Avoid all players following the ball.
Communicate rotations clearly.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players move automatically after disposal.
Whether important lanes are replaced.
Whether width and depth remain connected.
Whether players crowd the new ball side.
Whether defensive balance is maintained.
Whether rotations are communicated.
progressions: Assign player leaders to manage rotations.
matchApplication: Team structure changes every time the football moves. Players must continually replace space, maintain connection and preserve defensive balance rather than simply running towards the next contest.

title: Late Runner Recognition
objective: Teach players to identify late-arriving runners who enter space after defenders have committed to earlier options.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one ball carrier at the starting end.
Place two early targets inside the area with two defenders.
Position one late runner behind the ball carrier.
Mark a central arrival zone and two wider target zones.
The late runner may enter only after the first two targets begin moving.
howTheDrillWorks:
The early targets lead and attempt to draw defenders.
The ball carrier scans their movement and defensive reaction.
The late runner delays, then accelerates into the space created behind or between defenders.
The ball carrier may use an early target if that player gains a clear advantage.
If defenders commit to the early movement, the late runner becomes the preferred option.
The receiver continues through one additional disposal or shot.
Two points are awarded for correctly using the late runner.
One point is awarded for correctly using an open early target.
Rotate all roles after each passage.
coachingPoints: Late movement must remain patient until defenders commit.
Accelerate sharply when the space opens.
The ball carrier must continue scanning after the first options appear.
Early targets should clear or hold defenders.
Do not ignore an early option that is genuinely free.
Deliver into the late runner’s path.
Communicate the late movement without alerting defenders too early.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the late runner delays sufficiently.
Whether early targets influence defenders.
Whether the ball carrier stops scanning too soon.
Whether the late arrival attacks useful space.
Whether the disposal leads the runner.
Whether defenders pass runners between them.
progressions: Begin with a moving ball carrier.
successIndicators: Use the runner who gains the greatest advantage.
matchApplication: Late runners regularly become dangerous through the midfield and inside 50 because defenders have already committed to earlier leads, contests or ball-side movement.

title: Movement Chain Under Pressure
primarySkill: Maintaining coordinated movement across multiple possessions
objective: Develop players’ ability to make consecutive movement decisions while pressure, ball position and teammate roles change throughout a possession chain.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use two teams of five to ten players.
Position a scoring gate at each end.
Begin one team in possession.
No player may remain stationary for more than three seconds unless holding width or defensive balance.
At least one attacker must remain behind the football.
Defenders apply controlled match-like pressure.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team attempts to move the football through at least five disposals before scoring.
After each disposal, players choose whether to lead, overlap, hold, clear, fold or rotate.
The ball carrier must assess available space, pressure and support.
Defenders attempt to disrupt movement and force players into duplicated lanes.
A team receives one point for every five-disposal chain completed with clear width and depth.
Reaching the scoring gate adds two points.
A turnover creates immediate transition towards the opposite gate.
The coach may introduce a second football restart if play becomes congested.
Complete repeated two-minute blocks.
Review one movement decision between blocks.
coachingPoints: Scan before every movement change.
Avoid repeating the same running pattern after each disposal.
Maintain separate lanes around possession.
Replace space vacated by teammates.
Keep support behind unstable possession.
Use late movement after defenders commit.
Transition immediately when possession changes.
Maintain decision quality under fatigue.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether movement decisions remain connected across phases.
Whether players crowd the ball side.
Whether width and depth are maintained.
Whether late or overlapping runners are recognised.
Whether players replace vacated positions.
Whether movement quality declines under fatigue.
Whether transition reactions are immediate.
progressions: Increase contact to full legal match intensity.
regressions: Require only three disposals before scoring.
successIndicators: Make purposeful movement after every disposal.
matchApplication: Successful Australian football movement requires a chain of connected decisions rather than one isolated run. Players must continually update their role as possession, pressure and field position change.

title: Decision-Making Movement Phase Assessment
primarySkill: Integrated movement decision making under match-like pressure
objective: Assess players’ ability to coordinate movement before, during and after possession across the complete Decision Making movement-development phase.
groundSize: Half to three-quarter ground divided into defensive exit, midfield movement and forward-entry zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the playing area into three connected zones.
The defensive zone contains boundary, corridor and reset exits.
The midfield zone requires coordinated support, overlap and lane selection.
The forward zone contains leading, holding, clearing and late-run opportunities.
Use two balanced teams.
Position spare footballs around the area for rapid restarts.
Assign coaches or player leaders to record movement decisions.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins with possession in the defensive zone.
Players organise support ahead of and behind the football.
On entering midfield, players choose between carrying, releasing, overlapping, folding or holding shape.
Forward players coordinate early leads, decoy movement, clearing runs and late arrivals.
The attacking team scores three points for a goal or successful target entry.
One additional point is awarded for each clearly correct movement decision identified by the assessor.
The defending team scores for turnovers and successful counterattacks.
On turnover, both teams immediately reorganise into attacking and defensive lanes.
Coaches restart from different zones to vary the movement problem.
Play in four-minute blocks with one-minute review periods.
Rotate players through defensive, midfield and forward roles.
Complete at least four blocks before final assessment.
coachingPoints: Scan before moving and before receiving.
Decide whether to lead, hold, clear, overlap, fold or rotate.
Maintain separate lanes around possession.
Keep at least one player connected behind the football.
Use decoy and late movement to manipulate defenders.
Select inside or outside lanes according to defensive shape.
Replace positions vacated by teammates.
React immediately after turnovers.
Assess movement decisions separately from execution errors.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether movement begins after scanning.
Whether leading patterns remain coordinated.
Whether players select safe receiving paths.
Whether overlaps create genuine advantage.
Whether support remains ahead and behind possession.
Whether decoy and late runs affect defenders.
Whether players rotate into vacated positions.
Whether teams retain width and depth.
Whether transition lanes are filled quickly.
Whether decision quality survives fatigue and pressure.
progressions: Remove all marked zones and gates.
Increase pressure to full match intensity.
Begin from stoppages, kick-ins and intercepted marks.
Require player leaders to organise movement.
Record individual results across repeated sessions.
regressions: Assess one zone at a time.
Allocate one movement focus to each line.
Pause after selected possessions for guided questioning.
successIndicators: Coordinate leads, holds and clearing runs.
Select effective inside and outside lanes.
Use decoy and late movement purposefully.
Explain how their movement created or protected team advantage.
matchApplication: The assessment recreates the connected movement demands of Australian football from defensive exit through midfield progression and forward entry. It evaluates whether players can adapt their positioning and running patterns to the live game picture rather than relying on predetermined movement.

title: First-Pressure Release
primarySkill: Selecting the first disposal under immediate pressure
objective: Develop players’ ability to identify and execute the safest productive disposal when pressure arrives immediately after possession is won.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Position one receiver in the centre of the area.
Place a feeder eight to ten metres away.
Position one pressure player behind or beside the receiver.
Set three supporting targets around the receiver: forward, lateral and rear-release.
The pressure player varies the closing angle on every repetition.
Targets must remain in separate passing lanes.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver scans the pressure player and supporting targets before presenting.
The feeder delivers the football.
The pressure player closes immediately after the disposal is released.
The receiver must take possession and select the target furthest from the pressure line.
A forward release scores two points when it is available and safe.
A lateral or rear release scores one point when it correctly protects possession.
The pressure player scores one point for forcing a fumble, poor disposal or tackle.
Play continues through one additional disposal.
Rotate feeder, receiver, pressure player and support roles.
Practise pressure arriving from both sides and directly behind.
coachingPoints: Scan before possession so the first release option is already forming.
Identify the pressure angle, not only the pressure distance.
Release away from the defender’s momentum.
Use the forward option when it remains clear.
Do not force forward movement through a closed lane.
Keep the football protected until the disposal action begins.
Support players must provide clear width and depth.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the receiver scans before the football arrives.
Whether the selected disposal moves away from pressure.
Whether players panic and dispose without identifying a target.
Whether the forward option is used when available.
Whether support players maintain separate lanes.
Whether decision speed remains high without sacrificing accuracy.
progressions: Allow targets to move after the football is released.
Continue into live 3v2 transition after the first disposal.
regressions: Increase the distance between pressure player and receiver.
Allow the coach to call the safest target initially.
successIndicators: Select a release away from pressure.
Use forward options when genuinely available.
matchApplication: The drill replicates possession won at stoppages, ground-ball contests and congested midfield situations where the first decision must protect the football while preserving attacking momentum.

title: Contact-Side Exit
primarySkill: Selecting an exit away from body contact
objective: Teach players to identify the contact side and exit or release towards the side that provides the greatest protection and space.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Position one ball winner in the centre.
Place one contact player on either the left or right side.
Set an exit gate on each side of the contest.
Position one supporting teammate beyond each gate.
A feeder rolls or handballs the football towards the ball winner.
Contact must remain controlled and legal.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball winner approaches and collects the football.
The contact player applies controlled body pressure from one side.
The ball winner identifies the contact side as possession is secured.
The player protects the football and attempts to exit through the opposite gate.
If the exit lane closes, the player releases to the support target on the protected side.
The contact player attempts to delay without tackling during the first phase.
One point is awarded for selecting the correct exit side.
A second point is awarded for clean execution.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
Alternate contact sides and starting speeds.
coachingPoints: Lower the centre of gravity before contact.
Keep the football on the side furthest from the defender.
Use the hips and shoulders to absorb controlled contact.
Exit opposite the defender’s momentum.
Avoid spinning without first identifying clear space.
Release to support when the physical exit is closed.
Accelerate after separating from contact.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball winner identifies the contact side.
Whether the football remains protected.
Whether players maintain balance during contact.
Whether the exit direction creates separation.
Whether players spin blindly into another pressure area.
Whether support is used when the exit is unavailable.
progressions: Add a second defender beyond one exit.
Require a disposal immediately after separation.
regressions: Use bump pads rather than players.
Allow the ball winner to begin with possession.
successIndicators: Protect the football away from the defender.
Release effectively when physical separation is unavailable.
matchApplication: Players winning contested football frequently absorb pressure from one side. Recognising the contact line helps them protect possession and escape towards support rather than turning into additional pressure.

title: Blind-Side Pressure Scan
primarySkill: Recognising pressure outside the direct field of vision
objective: Develop players’ ability to detect and respond to pressure approaching from behind or outside their immediate vision before taking possession.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position a feeder at one end and a receiver in the centre.
Place two pressure players behind the receiver, one on each blind side.
Only one pressure player becomes active during each repetition.
Position three disposal targets ahead and to the sides.
The receiver may scan before and during the lead.
Supporting players may provide pressure calls.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver begins a short lead towards the feeder.
One pressure player is released from behind on the coach’s signal.
The receiver completes a shoulder check while moving.
The feeder delivers the football.
The receiver must take possession with a body position that protects against the active pressure side.
The player disposes to the target furthest from the pressure line.
The pressure player applies controlled closing pressure.
One point is awarded for identifying the pressure side and one for the correct disposal.
Rotate all roles after several repetitions.
Occasionally release no pressure player so the receiver must recognise genuine time.
coachingPoints: Scan both blind sides before possession.
Use a quick shoulder check rather than a full body turn.
Return the eyes to the football early.
Adjust body orientation to protect against the active pressure side.
Do not assume pressure is present merely because teammates call.
Use available time when no defender is released.
Dispose away from the defender’s approach.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether scanning occurs early enough.
Whether the receiver checks both sides over repeated attempts.
Whether the active pressure player is correctly identified.
Whether scanning disrupts the receive.
Whether body orientation protects possession.
Whether players recognise when no pressure exists.
progressions: Release both pressure players with one acting as a decoy.
Change the pressure side after the first scan.
regressions: Show the pressure side before the lead.
Allow the coach to pause before the receive.
successIndicators: Select a disposal away from pressure.
Use available time when pressure is absent.
matchApplication: Pressure often arrives from behind at stoppages, through the midfield and during forward leads. Blind-side scanning allows players to avoid tackles and make productive first decisions.

title: Two-Defender Trap Escape
objective: Teach players to recognise and escape a developing two-defender trap by attacking the available seam, releasing early or resetting possession.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one ball carrier at the base of the area.
Place two defenders ahead, separated by four to six metres.
Set a central seam gate and two outside release gates.
Position one support player behind and one on each side.
Defenders may converge together, stagger their pressure or leave the seam open.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier enters the area with possession.
Both defenders move to contain the player.
If the defenders separate or arrive at different times, the carrier attacks the seam between them.
If both defenders converge tightly, the carrier releases to an outside support player.
If outside options are blocked, the carrier uses the rear reset.
Defenders apply controlled legal pressure.
Attackers score two points for breaking the trap and reaching an exit gate.
Defenders score one point for forcing a turnover or stoppage.
Play continues for six seconds after the first decision.
Rotate carriers, defenders and support players.
coachingPoints: Recognise the distance and timing between the defenders.
Attack the seam before it closes.
Do not attempt to split defenders who are already connected.
Draw pressure towards the football before releasing outside.
Keep a rear support option available.
Protect the football through contact.
Accelerate immediately after escaping.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier recognises defender spacing.
Whether the seam is attacked early enough.
Whether players run into a closed trap.
Whether outside support maintains width.
Whether the reset remains visible.
Whether the carrier accelerates after the first action.
progressions: Permit full legal tackling appropriate to the group.
Add a third defender covering one release.
Begin with the carrier receiving an imperfect disposal.
regressions: Walk through the first few repetitions.
successIndicators: Maintain access to outside and rear support.
matchApplication: Ball carriers are frequently trapped near the boundary, after stoppage exits or during defensive pressure. Effective decisions depend on recognising whether a seam can be attacked or whether possession must be released before the trap closes.

title: Congestion Possession Choice
primarySkill: Selecting whether to possess, knock or release in congestion
objective: Develop players’ ability to decide whether to secure possession, knock the football to advantage or release it immediately in a congested contest.
groundSize: 12 × 18-metre contest area with two exit zones.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Use two teams of three or four players.
Place the football in the central contest area.
Mark one exit gate at each end.
Position one outside support player for each team.
The coach may roll, bounce or drop the football into the contest.
Contact must remain controlled and appropriate to the group.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players contest the loose football.
The first player to reach it scans pressure, support and available exits.
With time and balance, the player takes clean possession.
Under immediate pressure with support available, the player knocks or taps the football to advantage.
If possession is secured, the player releases quickly to an outside teammate.
Teams attempt to move the football through their attacking gate.
One point is awarded for a correct first decision.
A second point is awarded for a successful team exit.
Reset after an exit, stoppage or turnover.
Rotate outside support players regularly.
coachingPoints: Keep the eyes up for as long as possible when approaching.
Take possession when it provides control and an exit.
Do not take possession merely to be tackled immediately.
Knock or tap only towards visible support.
Protect the football with the body when possession is secured.
Outside players must communicate and stay clear of congestion.
Reassess after every deflection.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players scan before lowering to the football.
Whether clean possession is chosen appropriately.
Whether taps and knocks are purposeful.
Whether outside support remains available.
Whether players dive onto the football unnecessarily.
Whether teams react to deflections and loose possession.
progressions: Add a second football during selected repetitions.
Continue into a live transition game after the exit.
regressions: Practise take, knock and release actions separately.
successIndicators: Direct knocks and taps to teammates.
Use outside support to exit the contest.
matchApplication: Congested football requires players to judge whether possession will create control or invite a tackle. The drill develops team-first choices that help the football move beyond the immediate contest.

title: Tackle-or-Dispose Window
primarySkill: Recognising the final safe disposal moment
objective: Teach players to recognise when they still have time to dispose effectively and when they must protect possession or absorb a legal tackle.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one receiver in the centre.
Place a feeder eight metres away.
Position one defender behind the receiver at a variable starting distance.
Place two support targets ahead and to the sides.
Mark a release line approximately two metres from the receiver.
The defender begins only when the feeder releases the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver scans the defender and support targets.
The feeder delivers the football.
The defender closes from behind.
If the receiver has time before the defender reaches the release line, the player disposes to a support target.
If the disposal window closes, the receiver protects the football and prepares for controlled contact.
The receiver must not attempt a reckless disposal once balance and arm freedom are lost.
One point is awarded for a timely disposal.
One point is also awarded for correctly protecting possession when the release window has closed.
The defender scores for a legal tackle that forces an incorrect disposal.
Rotate all roles.
coachingPoints: Judge time from defender speed as well as distance.
Dispose before the arms become restricted.
Keep the football secure when the window closes.
Avoid throwing, dropping or blindly releasing during contact.
Use lateral movement to extend the disposal window.
Support players must present early.
Communicate whether the receiver is hot or has time.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the receiver recognises the remaining disposal time.
Whether disposals occur before contact restricts the arms.
Whether players attempt desperate releases after the window closes.
Whether possession is protected in the tackle.
Whether support presents early enough.
Whether defenders apply controlled legal tackles.
progressions: Allow the receiver to evade before disposal.
Continue live play after the tackle.
regressions: Predetermine whether the player has time.
Pause immediately before the contact decision.
successIndicators: Protect possession when the window closes.
Use movement to create additional time.
matchApplication: Players under closing pressure must know whether a disposal can still be completed legally and effectively. Attempting to release after control is lost often creates turnovers, while absorbing contact correctly can preserve possession or force a stoppage.

title: Smothered-Lane Reassessment
primarySkill: Reassessing after a disposal lane is blocked
objective: Develop players’ ability to abandon a blocked disposal and select a new option when an opponent closes or smothers the intended lane.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one ball carrier in the centre.
Place three target players forward, lateral and behind.
Position one pressure player three to five metres away with a smother pad.
The forward target begins as the apparent first option.
The pressure player may close the kicking lane, hold position or attack the handball side.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier receives from a feeder and initially assesses the forward option.
The pressure player moves to close one disposal lane.
If the forward kick remains clear, the player executes it.
If the kicking lane is smothered, the player withdraws the disposal and uses the lateral or rear option.
If the pressure player overcommits, the ball carrier may evade and reopen the forward lane.
One point is awarded for correctly abandoning a blocked option.
A second point is awarded for completing the replacement disposal.
The pressure player scores for a smother or forced turnover.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
Practise both right- and left-foot kicking situations.
coachingPoints: Keep scanning while preparing to dispose.
Do not complete a kicking action into an obvious smother.
Withdraw the football safely and regain balance.
Use a handball or reset when the kicking lane closes.
Recognise when an overcommitted defender can be evaded.
Protect the football during the aborted disposal.
Replacement options must remain visible and active.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise the closing lane.
Whether they can safely abort the disposal.
Whether the football is exposed during reassessment.
Whether replacement options are selected quickly.
Whether players evade when the defender overcommits.
Whether targets remain active after the first option closes.
regressions: Allow the ball carrier to begin stationary.
successIndicators: Reopen attacking play when defenders overcommit.
matchApplication: Players regularly prepare to kick before an opponent closes the lane. Effective decision makers can abandon the original action without panicking and quickly access a safer or more damaging alternative.

title: Outnumbered Contest Decision
objective: Teach players to make productive decisions when outnumbered by protecting possession, delaying the contest, gaining territory or creating time for support.
groundSize: 20 × 30 metres with a safe-side gate and attacking gate.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Begin with one attacker against two defenders.
Position one supporting attacker outside the area who may enter after three seconds.
Mark an attacking gate ahead and a safe-side gate towards the boundary.
The coach introduces the football through a roll, bounce or short disposal.
Defenders begin from different angles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker contests or receives the football while outnumbered.
The player assesses whether an immediate attacking exit is possible.
If no clean exit exists, the attacker protects the football and delays.
The player may move towards the safe-side gate to reduce turnover danger.
After three seconds, the supporting attacker enters.
The ball carrier must recognise when support has arrived and release.
Attackers score two points for reaching the attacking gate and one for escaping safely.
Defenders score two points for a turnover and successful counterattack.
Reset after an exit, stoppage or turnover.
Rotate all roles.
coachingPoints: Recognise the outnumbered situation early.
Avoid forcing a low-percentage attacking disposal.
Protect the football and make defenders commit.
Use boundary-side territory when it reduces turnover consequence.
Maintain balance and avoid diving onto the football.
Listen and scan for arriving support.
Release as soon as the numerical situation improves.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the attacker recognises the numerical disadvantage.
Whether the football is protected.
Whether the player forces an unnecessary disposal.
Whether territory is used intelligently.
Whether defenders work together rather than attacking from the same line.
Whether the ball carrier identifies arriving support.
progressions: Continue into live transition after the numerical balance changes.
regressions: Allow support to enter after one second.
Begin with the attacker already in possession.
successIndicators: Release when the numerical situation improves.
matchApplication: Players are often outnumbered near loose footballs, defensive exits and transition contests. The correct decision may be to delay, gain safe territory or create a stoppage rather than attempting an unrealistic attacking play.

title: Pressure Chain Continuity
primarySkill: Maintaining decision quality through repeated pressure
objective: Develop players’ ability to make consecutive effective decisions as pressure shifts from one ball carrier to the next throughout a possession chain.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use two teams of five to ten players.
Mark a scoring gate at each end.
One team begins with possession.
The defending team nominates one pressure player at a time.
After each disposal, the nearest defender becomes the next pressure player.
Attackers must maintain at least one forward, one lateral and one rear support option.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team attempts to move the football through the area.
The first defender applies pressure to the initial ball carrier.
After disposal, pressure transfers immediately to the next receiver.
Each receiver must re-scan and select an appropriate release, carry or protection action.
Attackers score one point for every three consecutive correct decisions.
Reaching the attacking gate scores an additional two points.
Defenders score for forcing a turnover, stoppage or poor decision.
After a turnover, teams immediately reverse direction.
Play in 60–90-second blocks.
Review the point at which decision quality or support structure broke down.
coachingPoints: Re-scan before every receive.
Expect pressure to shift with the football.
Support players must move as soon as the disposal is made.
Do not admire the previous action.
Use quick release when pressure arrives immediately.
Carry when defenders are slow to transfer.
Maintain support behind the football.
React instantly to turnovers.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether each receiver scans before possession.
Whether pressure transfers quickly.
Whether attackers maintain multiple support lanes.
Whether players use the same response regardless of pressure.
Whether decision quality declines during longer chains.
Whether teams transition immediately after turnovers.
progressions: Increase pressure to full match intensity.
Extend play across half a ground.
regressions: Limit the chain to three disposals.
Pause after each disposal during introductory repetitions.
successIndicators: Preserve decision quality across a possession chain.
matchApplication: Pressure rarely ends after one successful disposal. Effective teams continue making good decisions as defenders transfer, support angles change and the football moves through several players.

title: Pressure Decision-Making Assessment
primarySkill: Integrated decision making under pressure and contact
objective: Assess players’ ability to gather information, protect possession and select effective actions across varied pressure and contested-football situations.
groundSize: Half ground divided into four pressure zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Create four connected pressure zones:
Zone 1 – Immediate Pressure: Receivers must identify and use the first effective release.
Zone 2 – Contact and Congestion: Players decide whether to possess, knock, protect or exit.
Zone 3 – Trap and Smother: Ball carriers respond to converging defenders and blocked disposal lanes.
Zone 4 – Outnumbered Transition: Players delay or escape until support changes the numerical balance.
Divide the squad into two teams. Assign coaches or player leaders to record decision quality separately from execution.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins with possession in Zone 1.
The receiver must identify pressure and complete an appropriate first action.
The football progresses into Zone 2 through a controlled contact or ground-ball contest.
In Zone 3, defenders attempt to create a two-player trap or close the intended disposal lane.
Zone 4 begins with the attacking team temporarily outnumbered.
Supporting players enter after a variable delay.
The attacking team scores one point for each correct pressure decision.
A successful exit or score adds three points.
Defenders score one point for forcing an incorrect decision and three for a turnover followed by a successful counterattack.
On turnover, teams reverse direction through the zones.
Play in four-minute blocks with one-minute review periods.
Rotate starting roles and field positions between blocks.
coachingPoints: Scan pressure before possession whenever possible.
Identify defender distance, speed and angle.
Protect the football away from contact.
Use clean possession when it provides control.
Knock or tap only to visible team advantage.
Escape a trap before the seam closes.
Abandon a disposal when the lane is smothered.
Recognise when the safe disposal window has closed.
Delay intelligently when outnumbered.
Re-scan after every contact, fumble and disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players scan before receiving or contesting.
Whether contact-side exits are selected appropriately.
Whether possession choices suit congestion and pressure.
Whether players identify the final safe disposal moment.
Whether blocked lanes are abandoned.
Whether traps are recognised before they close.
Whether outnumbered players protect possession and wait for support.
Whether support players create useful release angles.
Whether decision quality survives fatigue and contact.
Whether teams transition immediately after turnovers.
progressions: Increase contact to full legal match intensity.
Begin from stoppages, kick-ins and turnover situations.
Require player leaders to organise pressure exits.
Record individual pressure-decision profiles across several sessions.
regressions: Assess one zone at a time.
Extend the time before contact arrives.
Pause between phases for guided questioning.
Give each player one pressure-decision focus.
successIndicators: Release before the disposal window closes.
Explain the reasoning behind their decisions.
matchApplication: The assessment recreates the changing pressure demands of Australian football, including immediate tackles, congestion, smothers, traps and numerical disadvantage. It measures whether players can protect the football while continuing to make productive team decisions.

title: Turnover First Action
primarySkill: Selecting the first action after winning a turnover
objective: Develop players’ ability to rapidly assess pressure, numbers and field position before selecting whether to attack immediately, secure possession or reset after winning a turnover.
groundSize: 30 × 40 metres with an attacking gate at each end.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Position a scoring gate at each end of the area.
Begin with one team circulating possession under controlled pressure.
The coach creates turnovers through an intercept opportunity, loose football, dropped mark or whistle-directed possession change.
Position at least one attacking option ahead, one lateral option and one supporting option behind the turnover location.
Use spare footballs to restart quickly from varied positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins in possession and attempts to retain the football.
The coach creates or signals a turnover.
The team winning possession must immediately scan pressure, numbers and available space.
If a clear forward advantage exists, the first action should attack the scoring gate.
If the new ball carrier is under immediate pressure, the team must use a safe release.
If forward and lateral options are closed, possession may be reset behind the turnover.
The team has six seconds to reach the scoring gate for two points.
A controlled possession that survives the first six seconds scores one point.
A turnover caused by a poor first decision scores two points for the opposition.
Continue play through successive turnovers before resetting.
coachingPoints: Scan before taking possession whenever the turnover is developing.
Recognise that the defence is often least organised immediately after losing the football.
Attack quickly only when numbers, space and disposal quality support the decision.
Protect the football when the first receiver is under immediate pressure.
Use lateral or rear support to improve the next attacking opportunity.
Avoid automatically kicking forward without identifying a target.
Players away from the turnover must spread immediately.
Reassess if the first attacking window closes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the turnover winner scans before disposing.
Whether attacking players spread immediately.
Whether forward options are used when a genuine advantage exists.
Whether rushed disposals are made into defensive coverage.
Whether support remains available behind possession.
Whether the team losing possession applies immediate pressure.
Whether the first action improves or damages the new possession.
progressions: Increase pressure to full match intensity.
Reduce the time available for bonus scoring.
Begin turnovers from defensive 50, midfield and inside 50.
Require two consecutive correct decisions before a score counts.
Allow immediate full-ground counterattack after possession changes.
regressions: Freeze play briefly after possession changes.
Provide clearly marked forward, lateral and rear options.
successIndicators: Attack when a clear advantage exists.
Secure possession when immediate attack is unsafe.
matchApplication: The first action following a turnover often determines whether a team creates a scoring opportunity or immediately returns possession. Players must exploit temporary defensive disorganisation without confusing speed with reckless disposal.

title: Boundary Trap Release
objective: Teach players to recognise whether to attack inside space, use a boundary-side release, create a stoppage or reset possession when trapped near the boundary.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark one long side of the area as the boundary.
Position one ball carrier within three metres of the boundary.
Use two supporting attackers against two defenders.
Mark an inside exit gate towards the corridor.
Set a forward territory gate along the boundary.
Position a reset target behind the football.
Defenders begin by blocking different combinations of the three exits.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier receives or collects the football near the boundary.
Defenders apply pressure designed to restrict space and trap possession.
The carrier scans the inside gate, forward boundary gate and rear reset.
If the inside lane is clear, the player exits towards the corridor.
If inside space is closed but forward territory is available, the player uses the boundary-side option.
If both forward exits are closed, the player resets possession behind the football.
When no legal disposal exists, the player protects possession and accepts a controlled stoppage rather than disposing blindly.
Attackers score two points for an inside escape and one for a safe forward or reset exit.
Defenders score two points for a turnover and one for forcing a controlled stoppage.
Rotate all roles and begin from both sides of the ground.
coachingPoints: Know the location of the boundary before taking possession.
Scan inside first because escaping towards the corridor can reopen the ground.
Do not turn blindly towards central pressure.
Use forward boundary territory when it reduces turnover consequence.
Maintain a rear release option.
Protect the football when no legal disposal is available.
Avoid handballing directly to a teammate standing on the boundary line.
Supporting players must create depth rather than crowding the trap.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players identify all three exit options.
Whether the inside lane is attacked when genuinely open.
Whether boundary disposals gain useful territory.
Whether support players maintain clear angles.
Whether players panic when both exits close.
Whether defenders coordinate to contain rather than overcommit.
Whether legal contact and boundary safety are maintained.
progressions: Permit full legal tackling appropriate to the group.
Begin from a boundary throw-in or loose-ball contest.
Continue play into full transition after escape.
Add score and time conditions requiring either retention or urgent attack.
regressions: Keep defenders in fixed blocking positions.
Begin with the ball carrier stationary and balanced.
successIndicators: Recognise boundary location and available space.
Escape inside when the corridor lane is open.
matchApplication: Boundary pressure reduces available space and can create predictable turnovers. Players must decide whether to escape inside, gain safe territory, reset possession or absorb pressure without giving the opposition an immediate attacking opportunity.

title: Corridor Collapse Decision
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise when a planned corridor attack has closed and select whether to change angle, use width or retain possession.
groundSize: 30 × 35 metres divided into a central corridor and two outside channels.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central corridor channel and two wider outside channels.
Use four attackers against three defenders.
Place a high-value scoring gate at the end of the corridor.
Place lower-value gates at the end of each outside channel.
Begin the ball carrier facing the corridor.
Defenders may leave the corridor open initially and then close it as possession develops.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession and assesses the corridor.
If central space is clearly available, attackers may move directly towards the corridor gate.
Defenders are permitted to collapse into the corridor after the first disposal.
The next ball carrier must recognise whether the central lane remains usable.
If the corridor closes, the team changes angle through an outside support player.
Attackers may later re-enter the corridor if defensive movement reopens it.
A successful corridor exit scores three points.
A wide exit followed by controlled retention scores one point.
A turnover in the corridor scores three points for the defenders.
Continue through the possession until an exit or turnover occurs.
coachingPoints: Reassess the corridor after every defender movement.
Do not continue with a planned central disposal when the lane has collapsed.
Move the football sideways or backwards to create a new angle.
Outside players must maintain width until needed.
Recognise when defensive collapse creates space on the opposite side.
Re-enter the corridor only when a genuine advantage reappears.
Keep support behind the football in case the attacking lane closes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players reassess after the first disposal.
Whether the corridor is forced despite defensive collapse.
Whether outside players hold sufficient width.
Whether the ball is moved quickly enough to beat defensive recovery.
Whether the team recognises a reopened central lane.
Whether rear support remains available.
Whether turnovers produce immediate defensive transition.
progressions: Add scoreboard scenarios rewarding either fast attack or controlled retention.
Begin from kick-ins or intercept marks.
regressions: Predetermine when the corridor will close.
Allow the coach to call the change of direction.
Use short kicks and handballs only.
successIndicators: Use width to change the defensive picture.
Re-enter the corridor when it becomes available.
matchApplication: Central ball movement can create rapid scoring opportunities, but the corridor may close while the football is travelling. Players must update the decision rather than continuing with a pattern that no longer matches the defensive shape.

title: Aerial Contest Ground-Level Choice
primarySkill: Selecting position and action beneath an aerial contest
objective: Teach players to read an aerial contest and decide whether to position front and centre, hold defensive side, attack the drop zone or remain outside as release support.
groundSize: A 25 × 30-metre area with one aerial contest zone and two exit gates.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one attacker and one defender in an aerial contest zone.
Place two ground-level players from each team around the contest.
Mark a front-and-centre zone, defensive-side zone and outside release zone.
Position a kicker 20–25 metres away.
Set a scoring gate for each team at opposite ends.
Rotate aerial and ground-level roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker sends a high football into the aerial contest.
Ground-level players scan the contest alignment, likely spoil direction and opponent positioning.
One player may position front and centre.
Another may hold defensive side to prevent an opposition exit.
A third may remain outside the immediate drop zone as release support.
If the mark is completed, the marking player selects an immediate or controlled next action.
If the football spills, ground-level players contest and attempt to exit through their scoring gate.
One point is awarded for correct ground-level positioning.
A successful possession and exit scores an additional two points.
Reset after an exit, mark, stoppage or turnover.
coachingPoints: Read the approach and body position of the aerial contestants.
Anticipate where a spoil or dropped mark is likely to travel.
Avoid placing every player directly beneath the football.
Front-and-centre players should arrive moving, not stand under the contest.
Defensive-side players must protect the most dangerous opposition exit.
Outside support should remain visible and ready for release.
Reassess immediately when the mark is completed or the football spills.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players occupy complementary ground-level positions.
Whether the likely spoil direction is recognised.
Whether players become stationary beneath the contest.
Whether defensive-side coverage is maintained.
Whether outside support remains available.
Whether possession winners release effectively.
Whether players transition when the opposition marks the football.
regressions: Reduce contact in the aerial contest.
Pause before the kick to identify required roles.
Roll the football from the contest zone before adding aerial play.
successIndicators: React immediately to a mark or spill.
matchApplication: Aerial contests are rarely decided only by the marking players. Effective ground-level positioning determines which team controls the spill, prevents an opposition exit and converts contested possession into useful ball movement.

title: Stoppage Exit-Side Recognition
primarySkill: Selecting the best stoppage exit side
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise the open, pressured and protected sides of a stoppage and select an exit that best suits the hit location and defensive setup.
groundSize: A 25 × 30-metre stoppage area with three exit gates.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use two ruck players and three or four midfielders per team.
Mark a front exit, open-side exit and defensive-side exit.
Position outside support players beyond each gate.
The coach varies the ball-up location and may nominate different ruck-hit zones.
Midfield defenders use different starting shapes to protect selected exits.
Contact must be controlled and appropriate to the playing group.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins with a ball-up or controlled ruck feed.
Midfielders scan the opposition shape and available exit space before the contest.
The ruck contest directs the football towards one of several hit zones.
The first possession winner identifies whether the intended exit remains available.
If the preferred side is pressured, the player uses a secondary release or protects the football.
Teammates block, support and spread into the selected exit lane.
A clean exit through the best available gate scores two points.
A safe possession retained under heavy pressure scores one point.
A turnover that exits through the opposite gate scores two points for the defending team.
Continue into live transition for six seconds after the stoppage exit.
coachingPoints: Scan the defensive shape before the ball-up.
Know the planned hit zone but remain prepared for an imperfect tap.
Identify the side with the strongest combination of space, numbers and support.
Avoid forcing the planned exit when the opposition has read it.
Use body position to protect the first possession.
Outside support must maintain width and remain connected.
Reassess immediately if the ruck hit misses its target.
Defenders should protect dangerous space before chasing possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether midfielders scan before the stoppage.
Whether players understand the intended hit and exit.
Whether the first possession winner recognises opposition pressure.
Whether the planned exit is forced when closed.
Whether outside support remains available.
Whether teammates protect the release player.
Whether both teams transition after the exit or turnover.
progressions: Increase pressure to full match intensity.
Begin from boundary throw-ins and around-the-ground stoppages.
Continue play across half a ground after the exit.
regressions: Pause after the hit for guided decision making.
Use one primary and one secondary gate only.
successIndicators: Recognise the most useful exit side.
Adapt when the planned hit or release is disrupted.
matchApplication: Stoppage plans provide structure, but the actual exit depends on the ruck hit, pressure and opposition positioning. Players must recognise when to use the planned side and when to redirect possession.

title: Front-and-Centre Action Choice
primarySkill: Selecting the first action after front-and-centre possession
objective: Teach front-and-centre players to decide whether to take possession, release immediately, snap at goal, gain territory or protect the football after an aerial contest.
groundSize: A 25 × 30-metre area with goals or three target gates.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one attacker and one defender in an aerial contest.
Place one front-and-centre attacker and one defensive-side opponent at ground level.
Position one supporting attacker outside the contest.
Set goals or target gates ahead.
A kicker sends the football into the aerial contest.
Vary the contest location so the front-and-centre player experiences different field positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker sends a high football to the aerial contest.
The front-and-centre player times movement towards the likely drop zone.
If the football spills, the player scans pressure, goal location and support.
With time near goal, the player may take possession and snap or kick.
Under immediate pressure, the player may release to outside support.
If clean possession is unsafe, the player may knock or soccer the football towards team advantage.
The defensive-side opponent attempts to pressure or win the spill.
Two points are awarded for the correct first action.
A successful score or team exit adds one point.
Rotate all roles after several repetitions.
coachingPoints: Arrive at the contest moving rather than waiting underneath it.
Read the likely spoil direction.
Know the goal and boundary location before collecting.
Take clean possession when balance and time permit.
Use support when pressure arrives immediately.
Snap or kick only when the scoring opportunity is realistic.
Knock or soccer the football purposefully when possession is unsafe.
Continue after the first action.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Timing of the front-and-centre run.
Whether the likely drop zone is recognised.
Whether the player scans before taking possession.
Whether scoring attempts suit the available time and angle.
Whether support is used under pressure.
Whether emergency knocks or kicks create team advantage.
Whether defensive-side coverage is maintained.
progressions: Use full legal aerial and ground-level pressure.
Vary the kick direction and spoil type.
regressions: Roll the football from the aerial contest.
successIndicators: Avoid low-percentage possession or scoring attempts.
matchApplication: Front-and-centre players can create scores or prevent defensive exits, but only when the first action matches the spill, pressure and field position. The best decision may be possession, release, territory or an immediate shot.

title: Deflection Recovery Support
objective: Develop players’ ability to rapidly change supporting positions and actions when a kick, handball, spoil or smother deflects the football away from its intended path.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Use three attackers against two defenders.
Position one initial ball carrier and two supporting teammates.
Set a target at the opposite end.
The coach uses a rebound board, smother pad or manual deflection to alter selected disposals.
Mark one attacking exit gate and one safe recovery gate.
Players do not know which disposal will be deflected.
howTheDrillWorks:
Attackers begin moving the football towards the target.
The coach or defender deflects a selected kick or handball.
All players immediately reassess the new football location.
The nearest attacker pressures or contests the loose football.
The next attacker provides a short release.
The furthest attacker spreads to an outside or forward recovery lane.
Defenders attempt to win the deflection and counterattack.
Attackers score two points for recovering and reaching the attacking gate.
One point is awarded for a controlled safe exit.
Continue play until a gate, turnover or stoppage occurs.
coachingPoints: Treat the deflection as a new possession phase.
Avoid continuing towards the original target when the football changes direction.
The nearest player attacks the loose football.
The second player provides immediate support without crowding.
The third player creates width or forward depth.
Communicate the changed roles quickly.
Protect against counterattack if the opposition wins the deflection.
Reassess field position before choosing the recovery exit.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Speed of reaction to the deflection.
Whether players continue following their original movement.
Whether the nearest player contests immediately.
Whether supporting players provide distinct short and long options.
Whether attackers protect against counterattack.
Whether the recovery decision suits field position and pressure.
Whether communication changes with the new picture.
progressions: Allow defenders to create live deflections.
regressions: Predetermine when and where the deflection occurs.
Practise with rolling footballs before aerial deflections.
successIndicators: Assign nearest, support and spread roles.
Select an appropriate attacking or safe exit.
matchApplication: Smothers, spoils, touched kicks and imperfect handballs create new game pictures instantly. Teams that reorganise first are more likely to recover possession and avoid being exposed on transition.

title: Repeat Contest or Spread
primarySkill: Selecting the next role after a contested phase
objective: Teach players to decide whether to remain engaged in a repeat contest, provide immediate support or spread away from congestion after the first contested action.
groundSize: 25 × 35 metres with three outside release lanes.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use two teams of five to ten players.
Begin with a central contested-ball situation.
Mark one short release gate, one wide spread gate and one forward gate.
Position at least two players from each team outside the initial contest.
The coach varies whether the first possession is clean, pressured or immediately spilled.
Contact must remain controlled and legal.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases a football into the central contest.
Players compete to win possession.
If the first possession is unstable or spills, the nearest players remain engaged in the repeat contest.
Players one step removed provide immediate support.
Players further away spread into wide or forward release lanes.
Once possession is secured, the winning team attempts to exit through the best gate.
The opposition applies pressure and protects dangerous lanes.
Two points are awarded for a clean exit after coordinated contest and spread roles.
Defenders score two points for winning the repeat contest and counterattacking.
Reset after a gate, turnover or prolonged stoppage.
coachingPoints: Do not leave the contest before possession is secure.
Do not send every player into the repeat contest.
The nearest players compete; the next players support; the furthest players spread.
Spread only when a teammate can reasonably release the football.
Protect dangerous space when the opposition wins possession.
Maintain communication about possession status.
Reassign roles whenever the football spills again.
Avoid standing between the contest and the release lane.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players identify when possession is secure.
Whether too many players leave or enter the contest.
Whether short support is available.
Whether outside players create width and depth.
Whether players re-engage after another spill.
Whether defenders protect dangerous space.
Whether decision quality remains under fatigue.
progressions: Reduce the size of the contest area.
Increase contact to full match intensity.
Continue into full transition after exits.
Begin from stoppages, marking contests and ground-ball situations.
regressions: Predetermine whether the first possession will be clean or spilled.
Mark clear contest, support and spread zones.
successIndicators: Remain engaged while possession is unstable.
matchApplication: Contested phases often involve several attempts before possession is clearly won. Players must balance repeat contest effort with outside support and spread rather than abandoning the football or crowding it unnecessarily.

title: Contest-to-Transition Chain
primarySkill: Connecting contested possession to structured transition
objective: Develop players’ ability to move from a contested possession phase into organised attacking transition while the opposition applies immediate counter-pressure.
groundSize: Half ground divided into a contest zone, release zone and transition zone.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the half ground into three connected zones.
Zone 1 is a compact contested-ball area.
Zone 2 is a short-release area with lateral and rear support.
Zone 3 is an open transition area with wide, corridor and forward targets.
Use two balanced teams.
Position spare footballs around the contest zone for rapid restarts.
Assign coaches or leaders to observe the first three decisions after possession is won.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins with a contested football in Zone 1.
Players decide whether to take possession, knock to advantage or protect the football.
Once possession is won, the team must complete an effective first release into Zone 2.
Supporting players spread into separate lanes in Zone 3.
The team in possession selects whether to attack quickly, use width or reset before transitioning.
The opposition applies immediate counter-pressure and attempts to force a turnover.
A successful transition into the scoring zone is worth three points.
One point is awarded for each correct decision during the contest, release and transition phases.
